subject: Re: Client-side consent signals — evidence for DPA / subprocessor scope
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme-retail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Hunt <privacy@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Client-side consent signals — what we need for DPA review

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. We’re kicking off our DPA review and need a concise description of how Redwood ingests client-side consent signals from our site (we use GTM + a lightweight Redwood browser SDK). Specifically we need: 
- a plain-language flow for how a user opt-out/consent choice goes from the cookie banner -> GTM -> Redwood (including any server-side hops),
- what data (headers, pseudonymous IDs, cookies) you persist or send to downstream subprocessors,
- whether any telemetry payloads include IP or user_agent in raw form, and
- an example event log (anonymized) showing the consent flag and timestamp.

We’d also like to understand whether you consider this a cross-border transfer (site in EU, Redwood ingestion in us-east-1) and what contractual/technical controls you apply (SCCs, encryption at rest, limited access).

Can you provide a one-page summary plus an export/log sample that we can attach to the legal review?

Thanks — Ben
Head of Product Ops
Acme Retail

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Olivia Hunt <privacy@acme-retail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Client-side consent signals — what we need for DPA review

Hi Ben / Olivia,

Appreciate the clear asks — attaching a concise export and a CSV mapping of telemetry fields (redwood-telemetry-mapping-2027-04.csv) along with a short DPA/SCC summary (dpa-scc-summary-202704.pdf). High-level answers below (TL;DR at the top).

TL;DR
- Consent flow: cookie banner -> GTM dataLayer -> Redwood browser SDK (or server-side collector) -> ingestion endpoint (us-east-1)
- Stored items: pseudonymous visitor_id, consent_flags (gdpr_consent: true/false), event_type, event_ts, and SDK metadata (sdk_version, region). No raw PII is stored by default.
- IP handling: IP is captured in transit to enforce geolocation routing but is hashed/trimmed before storage; IP is redacted in logs provided to customers by default.
- Cross-border: if your site is in EU and ingestion is to our us-east-1 cluster we classify this as a cross-border transfer. We offer SCCs + customer-managed key option or EU-hosted ingestion (private/dedicated) if you need to avoid transfer.

Shorter narrative (for legal):
- Client-side: when a visitor accepts or rejects tracking the cookie banner pushes a consent object to the dataLayer. The GTM tag triggers the Redwood browser SDK which includes the consent flag as part of the event payload (consent.{marketing,analytics}=true/false). If you prefer server-side tagging, GTM server events can be POSTed to our secure ingestion endpoint instead.
- Transport & persistence: events are sent over TLS to the ingestion endpoint. In us-east-1 we persist event metadata and an internal pseudonymous visitor_id. IP addresses are used transiently for routing and are not included in exported data by default.
- Subprocessors: we use a limited set of subprocessors for metrics ingestion and storage; the attached PDF lists current subprocessors and describes the SCC + encryption controls.

Examples included in the CSV: consent_flag,event_ts,visitor_id,event_type,sdk_version,geo_region
(anonymized row)  "gdpr:false,2027-04-10T18:02:31Z,visitor_7af9c3,event.page_view,js-1.4.2,eu-central-1"

Next steps from our side:
- I’ve attached the two artifacts above. If you need a full audit log or a SOC2 attest, we can share the SOC2 report under NDA. Marcus is looping in a couple technical follow-ups about field-level masking and retention (see his note below).

Attachments: redwood-telemetry-mapping-2027-04.csv (field mapping), dpa-scc-summary-202704.pdf (legal summary + subprocessor list)

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@acme-retail.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Hunt <privacy@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Client-side consent signals — what we need for DPA review

On 2027-04-11 09:34 -0700 Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> TL;DR
> - Consent flow: cookie banner -> GTM dataLayer -> Redwood browser SDK (or server-side collector) -> ingestion endpoint (us-east-1)

Hi Ben / Olivia — quick technical clarifications from engineering: 
- Field-level details: the SDK will include the consent boolean in the event JSON as consent.marketing and consent.analytics. By default we do NOT persist request headers like Authorization; we persist a minimal set of SDK metadata (sdk_version, lib_name).
- IP & UA: ip is available to our edge for routing and rate-limiting but we truncate IPv4 to /24 equivalent and IPv6 to a /64 before it’s written to persistent storage. user_agent is tokenized and only stored as a hashed fingerprint for UA-based routing (not reversible).
- Retention & masking: default retention for event metadata is 90 days; audit logs for compliance are retained for 1 year. We can configure retention down to 30 days for enterprise customers and add automatic field redaction for sensitive cookie values.
- Subprocessor exports: the attached CSV includes the current subprocessor set; we can provide an export with dates of subcontractor access for audit teams (requires an agreement).

If you can confirm whether Acme requires: (a) EU-only ingestion, (b) SCCs + CMK, or (c) field-level PII scrubbing in the pipeline, we’ll prepare the config options and a short runbook for your infra/legal teams.

Sample anonymized event (JSON for dev reference):
{ "visitor_id": "visitor_7af9c3", "event_type": "page_view", "event_ts": "2027-04-10T18:02:31Z", "consent": { "marketing": false, "analytics": true }, "sdk_version": "js-1.4.2" }

— Marcus

marcus_lin@redwood.com
